questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"For years, the village school had only one computer for two hundred pupils. Last year, a charity gave thirty laptops. The marks have not changed much yet, but the children no longer wait for hours, and their curiosity is awake."

What does the writer most strongly suggest about the gift?

options.text: It failed because the marks did not rise.
So far, it has changed access and motivation, not marks.
Technology always improves the pupils' exam results very quickly.
The school does not need any teachers now.

questions.explanation: The writer admits that the marks "have not changed much yet", then uses "but" to show the real gains: no more waiting and awake curiosity — access and motivation. "It failed because the marks did not rise" stops before the "but" and misses the positive part. "Always … very quickly" is contradicted by "not changed much yet", and teachers are never mentioned.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Every critic in the country praised the new film. But Maya left the cinema before the end, and during the film she looked at her watch three times."

What can we most reasonably infer about Maya?

options.text: She agreed with the critics.
The cinema was closing early.
She found the film boring.
She knew the film by heart.

questions.explanation: "But" sets Maya against the critics, and the clues — leaving before the end, looking at her watch again and again — show boredom. "She agreed with the critics" goes against the contrast linker and every clue. A closing cinema and knowing the film are reasons the text never gives: guesses, not inferences.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Parents often worry about screens. But a screen is only a tool: a wise user learns and stays in touch with friends, and a careless user becomes lonely. The problem is not the device but the hand that holds it."

In the last sentence, what does "the hand that holds it" mean?

options.text: the way each person uses the screen
the parents' real hands
the company that makes and sells the device
the size of the screen

questions.explanation: The expression means more than its words: the text opposes a wise user and a careless user of the same tool, so "the hand that holds it" is the person and the way they use the screen. Taking it word for word gives "the parents' real hands", which does not fit the idea. The company and the size of the screen are not discussed.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"At first, the new recycling rules seemed cumbersome: families had to sort their rubbish into four different bins. But after a month, sorting felt natural, and the streets looked much cleaner."

What does the word "cumbersome" most probably mean here?

options.text: cheap and very simple to follow
dangerous for health
fun and exciting
difficult and tiring to do

questions.explanation: "At first … But after a month" opposes the beginning to the end: sorting later "felt natural", so at first it felt the opposite — difficult and tiring. Four different bins is the clue of that effort. "Cheap and very simple to follow" goes against the contrast, and danger and fun are not suggested.

questions.prompt:
A paragraph opens with this topic sentence: "Reading for pleasure has many benefits for teenagers."

Which sentence should NOT appear in this paragraph?

options.text: It enriches their vocabulary and feeds their imagination.
It also teaches them patience and concentration.
The bookshop near my house closes at nine in the evening.
That's why readers often do better at school and in life.

questions.explanation: Every sentence of the paragraph must support the topic sentence. Vocabulary and imagination, patience and concentration are benefits, and "That's why…" is a closing sentence that sums them up. The bookshop's timetable proves nothing about the benefits of reading: it is irrelevant, so it should not appear.

questions.prompt:
Read this opening:

"Rude words turn small disagreements into real fights."

Which sentence is the most coherent and best-linked continuation?

options.text: That's why the bus to our school arrives at eight every morning.
While rude words start fights, polite words calm people down.
Because oil is very useful in the kitchen.
As a result, rude words help people become good friends.

questions.explanation: The opening speaks about rude words; the best continuation opposes them to polite words with a contrast linker: "While rude words start fights, polite words calm people down". "As a result, rude words help people become good friends" uses a consequence linker, but the consequence contradicts the opening. The bus and the oil change the topic.
